content:
- Model consistently underestimates true values, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecast tends to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increases — suggesting a lag or delayed response to recent price trends.
- After sharp spikes in history (e.g., 85+), model overreacts with exaggerated upward forecasts, then corrects — indicating overshoot bias.
- Model shows weak mean reversion: fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after volatility spikes.
- Forecast horizon 30d exhibits persistent downward bias, especially when history includes recent high prices — model fails to anticipate price correction.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price drops following high peaks — often misses the “rebound” or “reversion” phase.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window — may be overfitting to recent trends or ignoring volatility decay.
